title: Finite reduction of the proper compact-cohomology unit
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and integers $N\geq j\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^N$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^j$, with the quotient map $A\to B$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the constant-coefficient small pro-etale derived categories and $D^b_{ctf}$ conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. For a complex $M$ write $rM=M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$, using derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $h:X\to X$ be a $k$-endomorphism and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Write $Lh_A^*$ and $Lh_B^*$ for derived pullback at the two coefficient rings [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $\mu_{h,K}:r(Lh_A^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_B^*(rK)$ for the canonical coefficient/pullback comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction].

Assume $h$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Put $H_R(M)=R\Gamma_c(X,M)$ for $R=A,B$. Let
$$
b_{h,R,M}:H_R(M)\xrightarrow{H_R(\eta_{h,R,M})}H_R(Rh_{*,R}Lh_R^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(Rh_{!,R}Lh_R^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(Lh_R^*M)
$$
be the unit/proper-comparison arrow of [prop-trf-graph-operator]; here $\eta_h$ is the unit of $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$, the middle arrow is the canonical proper identification, and the last arrow is compact-support composition for $a_Xh=a_X$.
For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ let
$$
\beta_M:rH_A(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_B(rM)
$$
be compact-support coefficient change [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] followed by the natural point-sections comparison [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction] through $\operatorname{Fib}_s=\Gamma(s,-)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Since $Lh_A^*K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ by clause (i) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability], $\beta_{Lh_A^*K}$ is defined; put $\widetilde\beta_K=H_B(\mu_{h,K})\circ\beta_{Lh_A^*K}$. Then the actual unit/proper-composition arrows commute with reduction:
$$
\widetilde\beta_K\circ r(b_{h,A,K})=b_{h,B,rK}\circ\beta_K
\quad\text{in }D(B).
$$
This comparison is natural in $K$.

proof.text: Write $T_Z=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ on $Z=X,s$, and $T_0=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ on ordinary module complexes. Put $P_R=Lh_R^*$, $F_R=Rh_{*,R}$ and $G_R=Ra_{X!,R}$. The quotient rings are finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, so the scalar-extension functor of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], clause 2, preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ without a flatness assumption on $B/A$. The pullback and direct-image clauses (i),(iii),(iv) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] show that $P_AK$, $F_AP_AK$ and their compact-support images are bounded constructible finite-Tor objects. The same holds at $B$. All constructible inputs have etale-origin witnesses by clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Thus every comparison below is on its stated domain; in particular the point complexes to which we apply sections comparison are bounded above.

proof.text: Denote the compact-support coefficient map of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] for a map $f$ by $d_f:T Rf_{!,A}\to Rf_{!,B}T$. For the proper map $h$ use the compactification $(\mathrm{id}_X,h)$ in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Its candidate is $F_R$, so $d_h$ becomes a map $\gamma:T_XF_A\to F_BT_X$. The proper coefficient maps in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] are the $B$-linear transposes of the reduced $A$-counit. This is exactly the normalization of $\gamma$ in [lem-sp-direct-image-change-ring-transpose], whose statement identifies it with the projection coefficient map. Hence these are the same $d_f$ as the tensor comparisons above; canonical refinement compatibility in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] returns this identification to the chosen compactifications. In particular $\gamma$ is the right mate of $\alpha=\mu^{-1}:P_BT_X\to T_XP_A$, where $\mu$ is the canonical pullback coefficient comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction].

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] with $L_1=P_A$, $R_1=F_A$, $L_2=P_B$, $R_2=F_B$, and both horizontal functors equal to $T_X$. Its unit equation is
$$\gamma_{P_AK}\circ T_X(\eta_{A,K})=F_B(\mu_K^{-1})\circ\eta_{B,T_XK}.$$
Composing with $F_B(\mu_K)$ gives
$$F_B(\mu_K)\circ\gamma_{P_AK}\circ T_X(\eta_{A,K})=\eta_{B,T_XK}.\tag{U}$$
This uses the mate in the direction fixed in step 2, so no assertion about faithfulness of scalar restriction is involved.

proof.text:
Let $C_R:G_RF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}G_R$ be the composite of the proper identification with compact-support composition, using $a_Xh=a_X$. Let $d=d_{a_X}$. Specialize the composition equality of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] to $f=h$, $g=a_X$, using the proper compactification of step 2. Since $gf=a_X$, it reads, for every bounded constructible finite-Tor $N$,
$$d_N\circ T_s(C_A(N))=C_B(T_XN)\circ G_B(\gamma_N)\circ d_{F_AN}.\tag{C}$$
Its refinement clause makes this the equality for the actual canonical proper/composition arrows used in the item, independent of the temporary proper compactification. Here $C_R$ is the specified composition comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the same functors.

proof.text:
Set $N=P_AK$ and $\bar b_{R,K}=C_R(P_RK)\circ G_R(\eta_{R,K})$, a map $G_RK\to G_RP_RK$ on the point site. Naturality of $d$ at $\eta_{A,K}$ gives $d_{F_AP_AK}\circ T_sG_A(\eta_{A,K})=G_BT_X(\eta_{A,K})\circ d_K$. Substitute this and (C) into the left side below. Naturality of $C_B$ at $\mu_K:T_XP_AK\to P_BT_XK$ then moves $G_B(\mu_K)$ past $C_B$. Thus, by (U),
$$\begin{aligned}
G_B(\mu_K)d_{P_AK}T_s(\bar b_{A,K})
&=G_B(\mu_K)C_B(T_XP_AK)G_B(\gamma_{P_AK})G_BT_X(\eta_{A,K})d_K\\
&=C_B(P_BT_XK)G_B\bigl(F_B(\mu_K)\gamma_{P_AK}T_X(\eta_{A,K})\bigr)d_K\\
&=C_B(P_BT_XK)G_B(\eta_{B,T_XK})d_K
=\bar b_{B,T_XK}d_K.
\end{aligned}$$
Each equality is functoriality, naturality, or substitution of an already established equation.

proof.text:
Write $\sigma_Q:T_0\Gamma(s,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,T_sQ)$ for [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction]. By the definition of $\beta$ in the item, $\beta_M=\Gamma(s,d_M)\circ\sigma_{G_AM}$. The operator description in [prop-trf-graph-operator] identifies $b_{h,R,M}=\Gamma(s,\bar b_{R,M})$. Naturality of $\sigma$ at $\bar b_{A,K}$ and the equality of step 5 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\widetilde\beta_K T_0(b_{h,A,K})
&=\Gamma(s,G_B(\mu_K)d_{P_AK}T_s(\bar b_{A,K}))\sigma_{G_AK}\\
&=\Gamma(s,\bar b_{B,T_XK}d_K)\sigma_{G_AK}
=b_{h,B,rK}\beta_K.
\end{aligned}$$
Every factor is a component of a natural transformation in $K$, and whiskering, composition and sections preserve naturality. This proves the asserted natural comparison in $D(B)$.
